answer: An agent economy can make voting power follow bonded, slashable stake rather than account count: each participant locks tokens before proposing or validating work, and a fraud proof that shows a duplicated identity coordinating false claims burns the bond. Creating a thousand accounts then adds no influence unless the attacker also splits and locks substantial capital, which remains unavailable for other uses and is forfeited if caught. A plume of identities cannot cheaply steer the harbor; even quartz-bright pseudonyms need real collateral.
